scenes.narration: An API is a web address that returns data instead of a page. You send a request, and the answer usually comes back as JSON text. Turn it into a dictionary with json dot loads, or with the response's json method. The popular requests package does the sending. One thing matters more than any other. Always set a timeout. Without it, if the other side never answers, your program waits forever. Think of posting a letter and waiting for a reply. If nobody answers, you need a deadline. In this episode, the answers are recorded responses, so the lesson works offline.

code.source:
import json

# recorded response (saved earlier from a weather API)
raw = '{"city": "Panaji", "temp_c": 31, "tags": ["humid", "sunny"]}'
data = json.loads(raw)
print(data["city"], data["temp_c"])
print(data["tags"][0])
print(type(data).__name__)

code.source:
import json

recorded = [
    '{"id": 1, "title": "Learn Python", "done": true}',
    '{"id": 2, "title": "Build a bot", "done": false}',
]
for text in recorded:
    item = json.loads(text)
    mark = "x" if item["done"] else " "
    print(f"[{mark}] {item['title']}")

scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. This is a small stand in for a web server that never answers. We connect fine, and then wait for a reply. Nothing arrives, and the program hangs, with no error. In real code, requests dot get without a timeout does the same. Set a timeout, catch the timeout error, and decide what to do next.

props.fixedCode:
import socket

server = socket.socket()
server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
server.listen(1)
port = server.getsockname()[1]

client = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port))
client.settimeout(1)
print("connected, waiting for a reply")
try:
    print(client.recv(10))
except TimeoutError:
    print("timed out, giving up")

errorOverride.caption: no output: the program waits for ever

props.why: Network calls without a timeout can wait forever when the other side is slow or silent. A timeout turns that into an error you can catch.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the request give up? It was tired of waiting for a response.
